descriptionAdvanced.en: The Gualberto Villarroel Refinery is the cornerstone of Bolivia's energy processing infrastructure, located in the industrial zone of Cochabamba. As the country's primary refinery, it plays a vital role in national energy security by processing domestic crude oil and natural gas liquids into gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, and lubricants. The facility has undergone significant modernization and expansion programs in recent years to increase its processing capacity and improve the quality of the fuels produced to meet international standards. Operated by the state-owned oil company YPFB, the refinery is a major employer in the region and a symbol of Bolivia's efforts to industrialize its massive hydrocarbon reserves for the benefit of the domestic market.

en: The refinery has a current processing capacity of approximately 40,000 barrels of oil per day.
It is named after Gualberto Villarroel, a former Bolivian president who was a champion of national sovereignty.
The facility is connected by an extensive pipeline network to the oil fields of Santa Cruz and the Chaco.
It is one of the few refineries in the world capable of operating efficiently at an altitude of 2,500 meters.
